Description: Unique identifier assigned to each participant.
Unique identifier for a single trial within a session or condition.

The full five-digit DMDX item code of the trial: digit 1 the counterbalancing list; digit 2 the orthographic status (1 word; 2 pseudoword; 3 consonant string); digit 3 the visual overlap (1 low; 2 high); digits 4-5 the item number. trial_id is this code without its leading list digit.
Presentation order within the session (0-indexed). The order in which the participant saw this trial.

Duration in milliseconds for which the letter string was presented; thresholded individually for each participant in a preliminary task and therefore constant within a participant (33 | 50 | 67 | 83).
Experimental list number (1-4). Items were distributed across 4 lists; each participant saw exactly one list.
Type or category of the presented stimulus, such as word or pseudoword.
Experimental condition assigned to the trial.
The linguistic or visual stimulus presented to the participant in a given trial.
Number of characters in the presented letter string (4-6).
Position of the probed letter within the presented letter string (1-indexed; counted from the left).

Whether the probed letter sat inside the letter string (internal) or in its final position (external). The first position is never probed; external trials are always the last letter of a 4- or 5-letter string.
The letter that actually occurred at letter_position in the presented string; the correct alternative of the two-alternative forced choice.
The incorrect alternative of the two-alternative forced choice; the letter that occupies letter_position in the foil string selected by the trial's visual-overlap condition.
Mean human rating of the visual similarity between target_letter and distractor_letter on a seven-point scale; higher values indicate greater similarity (observed range 1.07-5.53).

Visual similarity between target_letter and distractor_letter derived from an HMAX computational model of visual cortex; the underlying scale runs from 0 to 1 and reaches 1 for a letter compared with itself (observed range 0.37-0.87).

The letter the participant reported. Not recorded in the source data; reconstructed from accuracy because the two-alternative forced choice records only correctness: target_letter on a correct trial and distractor_letter on an incorrect one. Carries no information beyond accuracy.
Binary indicator of whether the participant's response was correct.
Time taken by the participant to respond, in milliseconds.
